newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks fall, index at 42-month low.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks fall, index at 42-month low.

text.p: Singapore shares ended sharply lower on Monday with the benchmark Straits Times Industrials (STI) Index plunging to a 42-month low to end at 1,996.79, down 1.13 percent or 22.81 points.
"This is the lowest level the index has fallen. Since September 1993, it had always been trading above 2,000," an analyst with Singapore brokerage said.
Speculation that more bad news was in store for the Singapore stockmarket caused the sell-off, said dealers.
Rumours of yet more government curbs on public housing sent the property index down 2.39 percent to 657.04.
City Developments led the falls in active trade with a 70-cent drop to end at S$12.

UOB Foreign also shed 70 cents to hit a six-month low at S$13.40 with about 1.5 million shares traded. Dealers said some foreign funds were selling the bank. But a Keppel Sec analyst felt it was a good time to pick up UOB Foreign shares.
Industrial hardware maker Sin Soon Huat Ltd topped the active with over 44 million shares crossed at S$0.73-S$0.735.
Creative ended firmer at S$21.50 after the multimedia firm announced strong earnings for the quarter ended March 31 and said it expects better earnings in 1997. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083) REUTER
